source_name: LinkedIn - Fio banka company page
why_relevant: Purely Czech-owned bank with ~80 branches; its LinkedIn page is one of few public windows on hiring and internal moves at a bank that publishes little formal HR news.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Jan Juchelka (CEO & Chairman, Komerční banka; VP Czech Banking Association)
why_relevant: Top-of-house CZ banking executive who posts appointments and org news; his engagement graph is a reliable pointer to newly appointed KB executives before press releases.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Aleš Blažek (CEO ČSOB group, KBC executive committee)
why_relevant: CEO of the ČSOB/KBC group in CZ; self-reported org and leadership announcements, in Czech, typically ahead of corporate newsroom items.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Martin Vašek (Exec. Director home financing; CEO ČSOB Stavební spořitelna / Hypoteční banka)
why_relevant: Subsidiary-level CEO who posts operational/digitisation and team news; useful for detecting reorganisation inside the ČSOB mortgage and building-society entities.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Martin Podolák (Director of Product Management & Innovation / Deputy Director, mBank Czech Republic)
why_relevant: Mid/senior product leader at a foreign-owned CZ branch bank — exactly the lateral-move tier that never appears in press releases but is self-reported on LinkedIn.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Radek Trachta (Executive Director, Global Banking, Komerční banka)
why_relevant: Divisional executive at KB; his connections/comments are a snowball path into the corporate-banking layer of KB where reorganisations under the SG ownership change are likely.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Daniela Pešková (Board Member, retail banking, Česká spořitelna)
why_relevant: Board-level retail banking leader; board members announce their own mandate changes and welcome direct reports, giving early sight of retail org restructuring.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Lukáš Pešek (Open Banking, Česká spořitelna)
why_relevant: Open-banking/payments practitioner profile — the specialist tier that signals where a bank is building capability (PSD2/API/instant payments teams) through role titles and team-hiring posts.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - František Jungr (Head of Product CEE, Visa)
why_relevant: Scheme-side (Visa) CEE product leader based in the region; scheme and acquirer staff announce moves in English and are the connective tissue between CZ banks and payments vendors.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Silvia Mazanová (Chief Product & Growth Officer, payments platforms CEE/DACH)
why_relevant: Cross-border CEE payments executive; headline text itself is a self-reported role record, and such profiles broadcast new C-level appointments at CZ/SK payment platforms.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Jan Procházka (Bank Board member, Česká národní banka)
why_relevant: CNB bank board member self-reporting his regulator role; regulator-side personnel signals matter because CNB board turnover shifts supervisory and payments policy staffing.

source_name: LinkedIn profile - Kamila Šimonová (board member responsible for product development, insurer)
why_relevant: Surfaced directly by the Czech phrase 'nastupuji do' — a worked example that this exact self-announcement idiom is indexed and retrievable, and a bancassurance-adjacent move worth tracking.

source_name: X/Twitter - Air Bank (@Air_Bank)
why_relevant: Official CZ bank X account; occasionally carries recruitment campaigns and employer-brand posts, and replies expose employee accounts that announce their own moves.

source_name: X/Twitter - Raiffeisenbank ČR (@RaiffeisenCZ)
why_relevant: Official CZ account of Raiffeisenbank; same rationale as Air Bank — employer-brand and occasional appointment reposts, plus a discovery surface for staff accounts.

source_name: Bluesky - #Czech hashtag feed
why_relevant: Bluesky is the migration destination for part of the Czech professional/tech crowd; the firehose is openly accessible (unlike X), so it is the cheapest microblog channel to monitor, even though banking-specific volume appears thin.

source_name: e15.cz - tag 'personální změny'
why_relevant: Business daily tag feed collecting appointment stories across Czech companies including banks; a stable paginated entry point for backfilling moves first seen on LinkedIn.

source_name: NejBusiness.cz - Personálie
why_relevant: Explicitly frames itself as an overview of notable personnel changes in Czech and Slovak companies; low-friction open site, useful for mid-tier moves that national dailies skip.

source_name: Ekonom.cz - tag 'personální změny'
why_relevant: Weekly business magazine tag; lower volume but higher editorial weight, useful to confirm senior appointments that started as LinkedIn posts.

source_name: Médiář - Jobs
why_relevant: Médiář tracks people moves in the Czech media/marketing/communications ecosystem, which includes bank comms and brand roles; its jobs and people items are frequently sourced from LinkedIn posts, making it a pointer into individuals worth following.

source_name: Czech Fintech Association (ČeFiA)
why_relevant: Member/actor map for the CZ fintech and payments scene; membership and board listings give the roster of companies and named individuals whose LinkedIn/X accounts should be enrolled in this cell's follow list.

source_name: ČNB careers page (Zaměstnancem v ČNB)
why_relevant: Regulator's own hiring page; the counterpart to employee-advocacy posts on the supervisory side — vacancies signal where CNB is expanding supervision (e.g. payments/DORA/AML units).

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a evidence — nový portál MSp (verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Successor portal to or.justice.cz being rolled out by the Ministry of Justice; offers advanced search (rozšířené vyhledávání) across public registers, including search by person — the key capability for tracking an individual executive across multiple bank/fintech entities. Has an EN interface.

source_name: Sbírka listin (document collection of the commercial register)
why_relevant: Mandatory deposit of the underlying documents: rozhodnutí o volbě/jmenování/odvolání členů statutárního orgánu, zápisy z valné hromady, stanovy, projekt fúze/rozdělení, výroční zprávy. Since the 2024 přeměny amendment, merger projects and creditor warnings are deposited HERE rather than published in Obchodní věstník — making Sbírka listin the primary early-warning channel for CZ bank/fintech restructuring, typically ~1 month before approval.

source_name: Otevřená data veřejných rejstříků (dataor.justice.cz)
why_relevant: Bulk machine-readable (XML) exports of the full public registers, published in full scope since 2019 with periodic/incremental updates. This is the only scalable way to run automated diffing of statutory-body membership across the whole CZ banking/payments population without scraping the UI.

source_name: ARES — Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (web UI)
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance aggregator over the source registers (OR, RŽP, RES, registr plátců DPH). Single lookup by IČO/name returning identity, NACE, legal form and statutory-body data including start/end dates of each function. Fastest way to resolve a company name from press to a canonical IČO before pulling the register record.

source_name: ARES REST API + Swagger (vývojářské rozhraní)
why_relevant: Documented REST API (with an older XML interface still around) for programmatic retrieval of entity and statutory-body data — the sanctioned, non-scraping ingestion path for a recurring A5 org-change monitor. A changelog page documents breaking schema changes.

source_name: ARES otevřená data — katalog Ministerstva financí / NKOD
why_relevant: Bulk open-data distribution of ARES, catalogued both in the MF open-data portal and the national catalogue data.gov.cz. Useful for building a full CZ banking/payments entity universe (by NACE 64/66) rather than only monitoring a known watchlist — i.e. discovering subsidiaries and SPVs nobody has on the list.

source_name: Obchodní věstník (ov.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Official gazette carrying register entries, notices to creditors, convocations of valná hromada, liquidations and historically merger notices for CZ companies including banks and payment institutions. Full-text searchable by company name/IČO with publication dates — a dated, citable corroboration layer alongside the register itself. Note the domain migrated from ov.justice.cz to ov.gov.cz.

source_name: Insolvenční rejstřík ISIR (isir.justice.cz / eisir.justice.cz)
why_relevant: Statutory insolvency register; courts must publish within 7 days of proceedings starting, with continuous publication of decisions and submissions. For A5 this is the distress-side signal: fintech/payment-firm failures, forced management change, appointment of insolvenční správce — i.e. the most abrupt form of 'organization change' and a leading indicator of team availability on the CZ market. eisir.justice.cz is the newer front end.

source_name: Evidence skutečných majitelů (ESM) — esm.justice.cz
why_relevant: Beneficial-ownership register — historically the way to see who really controls a CZ payment institution or fintech SPV. CRITICAL STATUS CHANGE: the Ministry of Justice closed the public part and the ESM open data on 17 December 2025; access now requires datová schránka (own extract), JIP/privileged remote access for public authorities, or a formal request. Track it as a degraded/legally-restricted source, and rely on register ownership data plus commercial aggregators' historical ESM snapshots instead.
